HeroImpacto.subtitle: Traveling as part of a living process
HeroImpacto.text1: In Colonia Carlos Pellegrini and the Iberá Wetlands, traveling is not just about visiting a place. It is about becoming part of a process of territorial regeneration.
HeroImpacto.text2: Every visit leaves a footprint. Our commitment is to make that footprint positive, measurable, and shared.

TurismoImpacto.title: WHAT IS REGENERATIVE TOURISM?
TurismoImpacto.subtitle: Going beyond doing no harm
TurismoImpacto.text1: Regenerative tourism goes one step further than sustainable tourism.
TurismoImpacto.text2: It’s not just about “avoiding negative impact,” but about actively improving the places we visit:
TurismoImpacto.text3: In Iberá, tourism becomes a force for restoration, learning, and collaboration.
TurismoImpacto.text4: The goal is simple yet profound: to leave the territory better after every visit.

SunsetImpacto.title: HOW EACH EXPERIENCE GIVES BACK TO THE TERRITORY
SunsetImpacto.subtitle: Three levels of involvement
SunsetImpacto.text1: We design our experiences at different levels so that each traveler can choose how they want to engage.
SunsetImpacto.text2: The destination is the same. What changes is the way you experience it.

SkyImpacto.title: OUR COMMITMENTS
SkyImpacto.subtitle: Real, measurable and transparent impact.
SkyImpacto.text1: Our commitment is not just words. It is a certified and evaluated management system.
SkyImpacto.text2: Aligned with the Hoteles Más Verdes certification, we work with clear commitments:

options.title: Environmental commitments
items: Efficient use of water and energy

options.title: Social commitments
items: Free training programs for the community
Support for local entrepreneurs and producers

options.title: Management commitments
items: Partnerships with local and public stakeholders

SkyImpacto.text3: Visiting Iberá means choosing a form of tourism that cares, connects and regenerates.
SkyImpacto.text4: A journey that transforms the territory… and also those who experience it.

HeroDestino.title: THE DESTINATION
HeroDestino.subtitle: COLONIA CARLOS PELLEGRINI
HeroDestino.text: Where nature, community, and the future learned to regenerate together

MapDestino.title: A destination that is not visited:
MapDestino.subtitle: it is understood
MapDestino.text1: In the heart of the Iberá Wetlands, one of the largest and most biodiverse wetlands on the planet, there is a small village that has become a global reference for conservation, resilience, and human transformation: Colonia Carlos Pellegrini.
MapDestino.text2: What is now synonymous with thriving nature and conscious tourism was, for decades, a forgotten territory shaped by isolation, poaching, and a lack of opportunities. The story of this destination is not one of an untouched landscape, but of an ecosystem that learned to regenerate alongside its people.

HistoryDestino.title: History
HistoryDestino.subtitle: From forgotten frontier to a beacon of conservation
HistoryDestino.text1: Colonia Carlos Pellegrini was born as a rural settlement in an extreme environment, shaped by water, forest, and natural cycles. For much of the 20th century, Iberá was seen as an unproductive, marginal, and difficult place to inhabit.
HistoryDestino.text2: The creation of the protected area and, later, Iberá National Park marked a turning point: for the first time, the value of the territory was no longer in what could be extracted, but in what could be preserved.
HistoryDestino.text3: This change was neither immediate nor simple. It required decades of work, agreements, tensions, and collective learning. But it laid the foundation for a new identity: that of a community that chose to protect its environment as a way forward.

CultureDestino.title: Living Culture
CultureDestino.subtitle: Tradition that evolves without losing its roots
CultureDestino.text1: The culture of Pellegrini is deeply rooted in the Litoral region: shared mate, chamamé music, bonfires, horses, and a way of life shaped by water and climate.
CultureDestino.text2: Far from becoming a folkloric museum, the local culture remains alive and evolving.
CultureDestino.text3: Today, ancestral rural knowledge coexists with new generations trained in conservation and tourism, family-run hospitality ventures, and women and young people as key drivers of local development.
CultureDestino.subtitle1: Visitors do not just observe the culture:
CultureDestino.subtitle2: they take part in it, listen to it, share it, and respect it.

NatureDestino.title: Nature
NatureDestino.subtitle: A globally recognized biodiversity sanctuary
NatureDestino.text1: The Iberá Wetlands host one of the highest concentrations of biodiversity in South America. Here you can find:
NatureDestino.text2: Among them, a bird species stands out that exists only in the Iberá Wetlands, making this destination a key site for conservation and science, as well as a must-visit for birdwatchers from around the world.
NatureDestino.text3: Nature in Iberá is not scenery: it is a living system, monitored, protected, and constantly regenerating.
NatureDestino.bubble: Caimans, capybaras, marsh deer, more than 350 bird species, and reintroduced species such as the giant anteater, pampas deer, and jaguar
